comparison: Strong agreement on MYR1 dispensability for cell-autonomous survival in IFN-γ-activated macrophages (C5, C57, C65, C66, C88, C89). Both evaluations find the evidence convincing with appropriate controls. OpenEval provides detailed methodological assessment while peer reviewers accept without challenge, noting 'convincing evidence' for the paracrine mechanism.

Strong agreement on growth defect and rescue phenotype (C7, C68, C69, C70, C71, C90, C91). Both evaluations support the finding that MYR1-deficient parasites show growth defects that can be rescued. OpenEval emphasizes consistency across experimental systems; peer reviewers explicitly state 'convincing evidence' for in vivo rescue.

Strong agreement on independence from adaptive immunity (C9, C86, C87, C104). Both evaluations support the Rag2-/- mouse experiments showing rescue occurs without adaptive immunity. OpenEval validates the experimental design; peer reviewers note the paracrine effect 'works early - well before the development of adaptive responses.'

Strong agreement on paracrine rescue mechanism (C8, C12, C13, C78, C91, C95, C118). Both evaluations support the co-infection experiments demonstrating paracrine rescue. OpenEval emphasizes the low co-infection rate ruling out cell-autonomous mechanisms; peer reviewers accept this as a 'key role' of MYR1 in paracrine immune evasion.

Strong agreement on conceptual conclusions about MYR1 function (C11, C96, C103). Both evaluations support the interpretation that MYR1 does not primarily protect infected cells from immune clearance. OpenEval notes this challenges prevailing models; peer reviewers accept this as a major finding about paracrine mechanisms.

Strong agreement on cytokine measurements and paradoxical findings (C80, C99, C102, C105). Both evaluations support the observation that rescue occurs despite elevated IFN-γ levels. OpenEval emphasizes this strengthens the paracrine hypothesis; peer reviewers accept without challenge, noting early paracrine effects.

Strong agreement on cyst formation findings (C74, C75, C76, C113). Both evaluations support the data showing MYR1 is dispensable for cyst formation but important for dissemination/persistence. OpenEval notes low cyst numbers suggest important functions; peer reviewers accept these findings without challenge.

Both address cyst-related claims (C114, C115). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to alternative explanations not being excluded and speculative nature of dissemination hypotheses. Peer reviewers SUPPORT the findings without expressing concerns about alternative explanations, suggesting greater confidence in the interpretation.

Strong agreement on pooled screen discrepancy (C4, C55, C56, C92). Both evaluations support the observation that MYR1 shows minimal phenotype in pooled screens. OpenEval emphasizes this is well-documented by citations; peer reviewers accept this as established context motivating the study.

Divergent evaluations on paracrine masking in CRISPR screens (C20, C21, C97, C98, C121). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting claims are speculative and untested in other contexts. Peer reviewers also express UNCERTAINTY, with one reviewer 'not entirely convinced' initially, though concerns were addressed through discussion rather than additional experiments.

Partial overlap on CRISPR screen limitations (C20, C97). OpenEval SUPPORTS the conclusion about pooled screen limitations based on paracrine rescue data. Peer reviewers show UNCERTAINTY, with mixed responses about the 'paracrine masking effect' and concerns about controls, though ultimately accepting the discussion of this limitation.

Both address GRA12 control data (C67). OpenEval SUPPORTS the use of GRA12 as appropriate control showing IFN-γ-specific restriction. Peer reviewers SUPPORT in vitro characterization including controls without specific critique, accepting these as supporting context.

Partial overlap on growth defect characterization (C68, C69). OpenEval SUPPORTS these claims as part of comprehensive growth defect evidence. Peer reviewers SUPPORT in vitro characterization data without challenge, treating as established controls for main findings.

Minimal overlap on CCL2 and mechanistic speculation (C105). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature of effector mechanisms (C106-C112). Peer reviewers SUPPORT cytokine measurements including CCL2 without expressing concerns about speculative mechanistic interpretations.

Minimal overlap on hypothesis formulation (C19). OpenEval SUPPORTS the hypotheses as sound scientific reasoning motivating experiments. Peer reviewers address this tangentially in context of paracrine masking discussion, expressing some uncertainty about broader implications.

OpenEval evaluates extensive background knowledge claims (C1, C2, C22-C58, C100, C101, C107, C120) as SUPPORTED, noting they are accurately cited and establish necessary context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers typically do not explicitly evaluate background citations.

OpenEval evaluates methodological context claims (C14-C17) as SUPPORTED, noting they establish baseline expectations for pooled screens. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these represent methodological background rather than novel results.

OpenEval rates co-infection frequency claims (C93, C94) as UNCERTAIN because data are not shown in manuscript, preventing full evaluation despite importance for ruling out cell-autonomous rescue. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific concern about unpresented data.

OpenEval rates future research suggestion (C117) as UNCERTAIN, appropriately noting it is speculative and untested. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers do not typically evaluate speculative future directions.

OpenEval SUPPORTS the conceptual distinction between paracrine rescue and rhoptry injection mechanisms (C119), noting valid differences in contact requirements. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific mechanistic distinction.

OpenEval rates mechanistic speculation about multiple effectors and CCL2-mediated recruitment (C105-C112) as UNCERTAIN, noting hypotheses are reasonable but untested. Peer reviewers address cytokine data (R6) but do not separately evaluate the speculative mechanistic interpretations.
